Commentary.Commentary: Adios! Keshav Maharaj has been handed over the trohy. He walks away towards his fellow teammates to pose for the cameras. While the New Zealand women’s team celebrated a dominant 4-1 series victory behind a masterclass from captain Amelia Kerr, the men’s side was unable to replicate that success in their own series decider, as both nations utilised the opportunity to test their bench strength only for the clinical visitors to walk away with the silverware. That is all from this series. Hope you enjoyed the coverage. Cheers for now.

A special comeback! Keshav Maharaj, the skipper of South Africa, says it is a wonderful opportunity for these youngsters to understand what international cricket is about. Shares that a lot of them underestimated their side with so many young players, but to see the hunger, desire and passion and to come back from 2-1 is super special. Mentions this series shows the depth in the system. They lacked experience, but to see the guys play today, it felt like an easy transition into international cricket despite some pressure behind them.

Opportunity for the youngsters! James Neesham, the New Zealand captain, acknowledges that the series has had its ups and downs, with the team fighting back in games two and three to take a 2-1 lead, but ultimately falling short due to subpar performances at the end of the series, which is disappointing given the long summer they've had since October. He notes that the scheduling is challenging, with cricket on at all times of the year, but believes that the opportunity for young players to gain experience is valuable, and that the team has seen some good moments and tough options, with the young players likely to take away valuable experience to improve themselves. He feels that the team has batted and bowled okay, but the fielding has been below par, and that South Africa's quality bowling attack has given their batters a taste of the next level.

Backing his instincts! For his career-best score today and a total of 200 runs across the five matches, Connor Esterhuizen wins the Player of the Match and the Player of the Series! Connor expressed his gratitude and credited his team's top-order batters for setting a solid platform, allowing him to play freely. He recalls ball striking to natural instincts and was pleased once they got past the score of 160-170, feeling confident that crossing it would make it challenging for the opposing team. Adds that the ball travelled nicely and the outfield was really quick. If red-ball cricket helped him in this format, Connor says it is a great back-to-basics format that helps you in T20 cricket. On playing for the country, Connor says they dream of playing for South Africa and adds that it is a special and humbling feeling.
...Presentation...

New Zealand failed to show up - The Black Caps’ struggle in the field set the stage for a difficult chase, having conceded a few too many runs in the first innings, and their response with the bat saw them falter completely. Already hampered by an inexperienced batting lineup, New Zealand desperately needed a solid platform, but instead found themselves reeling at 69/4 after a disastrous start. While Bevon Jacobs injected some much-needed impetus with a brisk 36 off 19 balls, his efforts weren't enough to repair the damage. The final blow to the Kiwis' hopes came with the dismissal of their skipper, James Neesham, which effectively ended the resistance. South Africa’s bowling unit was clinical in defense, while Gerald Coetzee, Wiaan Mulder, and Ottniel Baartman all finished with two wickets apiece. It was the overall discipline and collective execution from the visitors that smothered the chase and secured the series.

Proteas' charge with the bat! Despite the ball moving significantly early on, the Proteas showed immense composure to navigate the powerplay, losing just a single wicket. While the 55-run stand between Wiaan Mulder and Rubin Hermann provided the necessary stability, it was the explosive partnership between Dian Forrester and Connor Esterhuizen that ultimately took the game away from the Black Caps.  Their aggressive middle-order charge effectively killed the contest as South Africa ended with plenty on board despite the conditions helping the bowlers.

South Africa completes a comeback - Rising from a 2-1 deficit to clinch the series 3-2, South Africa completed a brilliant turnaround with a clinical performance against New Zealand under challenging conditions. This 3-2 comeback isn't just a series win, it’s a historic breakthrough for the Proteas. This marks South Africa’s first away bilateral series victory since August 2022, ending a long drought on foreign soil.

Commentary.Commentary: This spins away, on a good length, on off. Dane rocks back to punch it away but mistimes it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: George Linde to Dane Cleaver, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Slows it down, full and down leg. Dane gets down on a knee for the sweep but does not connect. Third wide of the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: George Linde to Dane Cleaver, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Low full toss, on middle. Robinson knocks it to long off and gets to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: George Linde to Tim Robinson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nearly sneaked through! This keeps sliding on with the arm, at the sticks. Tim goes back to a full ball but manages to keep it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: George Linde to Tim Robinson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good stop! Shorter and on off, a bit of extra bounce. Dane hops back to punch it away. Jason Smith slides to his left at extra cover and cuts it off. Just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: George Linde to Dane Cleaver, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Fired down leg again, Cleaver fails to get the sweep away. Wide given.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: George Linde to Dane Cleaver, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Sprayed down leg, full in length. Dane Cleaver sweeps but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: George Linde to Dane Cleaver, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Floated up, around off. Dane brings out the reverse but fails to connect. He gets rapped on the pads but well outside the line of the off stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: George Linde to Dane Cleaver, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: George Linde is brought into the attack.
A single to end an eventful over. Full and on middle. Dane Cleaver squeezes out an inside edge to mid on and takes a single to keep the strike. 17 runs off the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Wiaan Mulder to Dane Cleaver, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely done! Mulder goes back to bowling it short, on off. Dane Cleaver backs away and waits for the ball to arrive. He gets under it and plays the upper cut over the keeper for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Wiaan Mulder to Dane Cleaver, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Easy pickings! Too straight, full and sliding onto the pads. Dane Cleaver does not miss out on putting it away. Smears it to the right of the man at short fine leg for a four.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Wiaan Mulder to Dane Cleaver, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! ANOTHER CHANCE! Mulder stays short, on off. Dane makes room and throws the kitchen sink at it. The ball flies off a thickish outside edge to short third, where Gerald Coetzee leaps and sticks out his right hand over his head. He can only get fingertips to it before the ball races away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Wiaan Mulder to Dane Cleaver, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED AGAIN! Mulder bends his back and goes short, on off, Dane flays at it. Dian Forrester runs across to his left at deep backward point and extends his hands out in front but the ball drops on him. The ball clips his fingertips and goes down.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Wiaan Mulder to Dane Cleaver, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, on off, Dane Cleaver walks across the stumps and plays the scoop. He gets enough bat on it to clear the backtracking Ottneil Baartman at short fine leg. Dane collects a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Wiaan Mulder to Dane Cleaver, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED! Jason Smith shells it. On top of off, on a good length. Cleaver jumps out of the crease and throws his hands at the ball. Hits it straight to cover, where the ball dips on Smith, but he had it covered as he dived forward. The ball bursts through his hands and goes behind. Single taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Gerald Coetzee to Dane Cleaver, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A sharp and quick bumper at the bodyline of the batter. Dane Cleaver ducks under it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Gerald Coetzee to Dane Cleaver, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Around leg, on a short of a length. Tim shovels it down to deep fine leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Gerald Coetzee to Tim Robinson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another swing and a miss! Bashes the hard length, does Coetzee, over off and middle. Tim stays leg side of the ball and has a hoick across the line, only to miss.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Gerald Coetzee to Tim Robinson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Not far away from crashing into the stumps! Wobble seam ball at 148 kph, on a good length, on off. Robinson stays rooted to the crease and swings for the hills. The ball cuts back in to beat the inside edge but the bounce takes it over the off stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Gerald Coetzee to Tim Robinson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the channel, on a good length, Cleaver dances down the track to go big on the leg side. Miscues it off the inner half to mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Gerald Coetzee to Dane Cleaver, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Into the wicket, on middle. Tim keeps it out off the back foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Wiaan Mulder to Tim Robinson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Stand and deliver! In and around the off stump, on a back of a length, Robinson stands tall and lofts it with a high elbow to the right of mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Wiaan Mulder to Tim Robinson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Slightly too straight, at the hips. Cleaver is beaten on the flick. The ball goes off the pads behind square leg for a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Wiaan Mulder to Dane Cleaver, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Dane Cleaver walks in at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Strangled down leg. An innocuous delivery, but Wiaan Mulder will take it. Sliding down leg, on a length. Clarke has a swing at it to get it away. The ball catches his gloves before going behind to the keeper. Connor Esterhuizen moves to his left and gobbles it up with ease. New Zealand are 11/1, chasing 188.
Commentary.Howout: c Connor Esterhuizen b Wiaan Mulder
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Wiaan Mulder to Katene Clarke, OUT! c Connor Esterhuizen b Wiaan Mulder.

Commentary.Commentary: Tucking the batter up for room with a good-length delivery. Tim nurdles it behind square leg and crosses over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Wiaan Mulder to Tim Robinson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Moving away in the air, on a good length, Robinson gets on top of the bounce and punches it wide of deep cover for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Wiaan Mulder to Tim Robinson, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Wiaan Mulder to share the attack.

Drifting onto the pads, on the fuller side. Robinson brings his wrists into play and works it through square leg. The ball does not have enough legs to reach the fence, and the deep fine leg fielder mops it up. Three runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Gerald Coetzee to Tim Robinson, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on off. Katene advances and firms the drive in front of mid off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Gerald Coetzee to Katene Clarke, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angled into the right-hander, on a hard length. Clarke stabs it down on the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Gerald Coetzee to Katene Clarke, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and a hint of away shape, on off and middle. Tim Robinson moves away from the stumps towards the leg side and has a swing across the line. Miscues it off a leading edge over point. The deep third fielder gets around and slides to push the ball away from the fence. He saves a run for his side. Tim is off the mark with three runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Gerald Coetzee to Tim Robinson, 3 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Ouch, a painful blow! Extra bounce on display again, on a nagging length, on middle. Tim Robinson hangs back to deal with it but the ball nips back a touch to beat him on the inside edge and catches him on the box. Robinson is quick to get back up on his feet.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Gerald Coetzee to Tim Robinson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Clarke and New Zealand are away with a quick single. Gerald Coetzee hits the deck hard and gets the ball to deck away with a bit of lift from the surface. Katene rises with the bounce and drops it on the off side before hurrying to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Gerald Coetzee to Katene Clarke, 1 run.
